question: Was the pandemic tourism collapse by itself sufficient to cause Sri Lanka's 2022 external-debt suspension?
mechanism: Tourism removed a major foreign-exchange inflow, but a sufficiency claim must survive the 2019 tourism-only control case and separate pre-existing fiscal/debt vulnerabilities and later policy shocks.
transmission_channel: tourism receipts/foreign-exchange shock interacting with fiscal and external-financing constraints
time_lag: Easter shock 2019; pandemic shock 2020–2021; debt-service suspension April 2022
confounders: 2019 tax reductions and structural revenue weakness
commercial foreign-currency debt and maturity profile
Easter 2019 tourism shock and partial recovery
bounded_by: Refutes 'Covid tourism shock alone caused the default'. It does not assign causal weights among tourism, fiscal, monetary, agricultural, remittance and debt channels.
